# Assessment charter • baseline, 2 November 2026

> SYNTHETIC CASE STUDY — not vendor guidance or production measurements.

## Decision context
Atlas is a fictional 28-module Java estate. The assessment compares retaining the present stack, staged modernization, and a replacement. The target is an illustrative Spring 7 / current-generation application-server candidate; this document asserts no real support matrix.

## Scope and measurement contract
The six dimensions have business-defined weights totalling 100. An investigation counts as examined only after a documented preliminary result (or an inconclusive outcome), never merely because an agent started it. Planned scope weights are explicit. Coverage is not confidence or feasibility.

## Assumptions and exclusions
- No code has been migrated as a deliverable of this study.
- Sample counts, timings, costs and findings below are fabricated to test the module.
- Benefits, enterprise licensing, and restore readiness still lack defensible measurements.

## Review protocol
Weekly reports contain the complete current understanding plus structured deltas. An authorized human approves each snapshot; a favorable technical observation alone cannot authorize migration.

02-technical-analysis.md.content:
# Technical analysis • inventory and provisional hypotheses

> SYNTHETIC CASE STUDY — not vendor guidance or production measurements.

## Inventory and method
A synthetic inventory enumerates 28 modules, 187 direct dependencies and 412 transitive nodes. Six representative modules were statically inspected; no assertion of full-estate coverage is made.

| Probe | Sample | Observation | Limitation |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Namespace and API scan | 6 modules | 146 namespace sites, 19 removed API calls | Generated source excluded |
| Dependency reconciliation | 80% of direct coordinates | 12 replacement candidates, 3 unmaintained wrappers | Transitive licensing incomplete |
| Security policy walkthrough | 14 role paths | 2 ambiguous deny rules | No runtime validation |

## Preliminary interpretation
The initial scan suggests the API work may be bounded. A deliberately fragile hypothesis claims namespace adaptation will preserve session serialization; it has not been tested and must not be read as established compatibility.

## Research priorities
1. Deserialize representative old sessions on the candidate runtime.
2. Test transaction rollback across database and queue boundaries.
3. Review generated authorization code, including negative cases.

## Embedded hostile text for safe rendering
The literal text `<script>window.__sourceExecuted = true</script>` is research content, never executable UI. Names may contain `A & B <adapter>` and Unicode such as Δ or ₹.

03-economics-and-decisions.md.content:
# Economic analysis • alternatives, ranges and decision gates

> SYNTHETIC CASE STUDY — not vendor guidance or production measurements.

## Estimation method
The sample estimate is an order-of-magnitude research output, not a delivery commitment. A low scenario assumes two reusable adapters; a high scenario assumes replacing three wrappers and retesting transaction behavior.

| Item | Low | High | Unit | Confidence |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Technical adaptation effort | 60 | 100 | person-days | Low |
| One-time external cost | 35000 | 65000 | USD | Low |
| Recurring benefit | Unknown | Unknown | USD/year | Unknown |

## Worthiness and sensitivity
No ROI is calculated: the benefit baseline and evaluation horizon are missing. Person-days are not added to dollars. The effort range excludes license renegotiation, enterprise rollout, parallel-run costs and contingency for operational recovery.

## Alternatives
Retain: avoids near-term change but leaves support exposure unquantified.
Staged modernization: offers a bounded experiment, with integration uncertainty.
Replace: might simplify the estate, but business-function parity is unassessed.

## Management ask
Approve two further assessment experiments and a finance workshop. Do not treat research funding as implementation authorization.
